## POS-Cattle | Integration of novel phenotyping and omics approaches for the sustainable management and breeding of autochthonous cattle genetic resources

## Research team and collaboration

POS-Cattle was coordinated by
[Prof. Stefania Dall'Olio](https://www.unibo.it/sitoweb/stefania.dallolio/en).

Research activities involved members of the
[Animal and Food Genomics Group](https://site.unibo.it/animal-and-food-genomics/en),
led by [Prof. Luca Fontanesi](https://www.unibo.it/sitoweb/luca.fontanesi/en),
and collaborators from the University of Parma.

## Project overview

POS-Cattle investigated the integration of
novel phenotyping approaches and molecular
data for the characterization of Italian
autochthonous cattle breeds.

The project focused on genetic resources
including Reggiana and Modenese cattle,
combining genomic and molecular information
to characterize biological variability
and traits relevant to sustainable breeding.

These activities contribute to understanding
the genetic and molecular characteristics
of local cattle populations and their
potential use in genetic resource management.


## My research contribution

My involvement in POS-Cattle is associated
with the computational analysis and
interpretation of genomic and molecular
datasets from local cattle populations.

The research context involves the integration
of novel phenotypes and omics information
to investigate biological variability
and support the characterization of
autochthonous cattle genetic resources.

My specific analytical contributions
and methodological outputs will be
detailed as they are documented.
